title: Chapter 1085
paragraphs: Chapter 1085
Episode 255. The Death of Kelliark Zipple, and....(2)
As if a shed skin were collapsing.

The corpse of the Kelliark Zipple that had opened the dimensional gate was splitting left and right. The Kelliark Zipple of the 33rd dimension who appeared from within was now the last remaining Kelliark Zipple across all dimensions.
A face as young and pale as Jin's; Kelliark's gaze met Jin's.
At that moment, Jin immediately realized it.
That he could not win against him now.

-[I'm sure. Anyway, the information delivery is about done. In any case, this world's Kelliark is such a dud. Getting pushed around by someone like Rokia. The Kelliarks I remember were much stronger. One of them in particular... he was absolutely formidable.]
He recalled what Orgal had said. The Kelliark who had just appeared was surely him.
“...You must be the leader of the Demon Army.”
Kelliark did not answer right away and cracked his neck as if stretching.

Even so, Jin could not recklessly attack him. An intuition, a powerful intuition that a single failed attack could lead to a fatal wound, that he could even lose his life, was sending a warning to his body and mind.

“That's right, Jin Runcandel. You look cleaner than I had thought. You must have gone through all sorts of hellish battlefields in this world, so I thought you'd look rougher, but a fine face without a single scar...”
Chit-!
Suddenly, a drop of blood flew from Jin's cheek as if a blade had grazed it. If Jin hadn't instinctively used his footwork, his neck would have been severed.
What had just left a wound on Jin's face was a spatial explosion at its peak. It wasn't flashy like the ones the Kelliark who had just died used, but it was dozens of times more threatening.

“But one should not judge a person by their cover. You are indeed the one who has drawn me to this shabby dimension, Jin Runcandel. That just now was a surprise attack with my sincere feelings, in its own way.”
Strong.
To an extent he had never experienced from anyone or anything before, even including Chiron and Van.
It felt as if the enemy's blade was touching his neck, his spine, his entire body. Jin raised his senses to their absolute limit and watched him.

The roar of explosions that had been ringing across the battlefield without rest since the fight began was subsiding. Even those who could not see this situation with their own two eyes were realizing that some immense being had appeared on the battlefield.
They had no choice but to realize it.
Because from the moment he appeared, all the functions of the Golden Fleet were ceasing, as if a river had been blocked by a wall.
The power sources sputtered, barely maintaining the fleet's flotation, and the shields all vanished as if magical lamps were being turned off.
The crew members who were not specially trained were grabbing their own necks as if they were suffocating, their bodies bending over.

Even the numerous Origin Stones that had appeared when the Holy Land unfolded had stopped their wailing, so it was hard to believe even while seeing that all of this was a phenomenon caused by the appearance of a single person.
[What in the world... is that... abomination...!]
Even Kragos, who had been under pressure from Van and the coalition members, lowered his head to look at the leader of the Demon Army.
A power so great it was impossible to believe it was his own creation.
He had already felt it while facing Van, but this was even more shocking. That mortal was, certainly, a 'hybrid' who had gained his vast power by devouring him and his brothers.
It was as if time had stopped.
For about ten seconds, the battlefield was engulfed in silence, and no one moved. Even the golden sea remaining near the Holy Land was completely still, as if it were stagnant water.
He was of a different caliber.

He was far beyond the standards of the mortal world. For instance, like the rank of a highest-tier god or a Genesis Knight, he could never be explained by the standards of the mortal world that had been used until now.
Right now, Jin was facing that great being at the closest distance, alone. Only the Genesis Knights could accomplish that task.
A cold sweat was drenching his entire body. The leader of the Demon Army, as if he had finished stretching, slowly took one step at a time towards Jin.
Anyone else would have had to step back.
However, Jin did not retreat, staring at him as he approached. Rather, he gripped his sword even more tightly.
Because he could not refuse to fight just because he could not win.
'As things stand, he is an opponent for whom no answer comes to mind. For now, the best move is to retreat somehow... but I cannot do so without clashing even once.'
To retreat his entire force, including himself, without taking any damage against that monster.
That was absolutely impossible. Unless, for no reason at all, the leader of the Demon Army were to suddenly commit suicide, absolutely not.
He had to be aware of Kelliark striding towards him now, be aware of that truly perfected spatial explosion, and grasp the intention of Malugia, the one who had orchestrated this situation.
And while doing all that, he had to find the path that would allow him to retreat his allies most effectively.

'There is surely an intention behind Malugia making that man appear here. There must have been some kind of fight between Malugia and the leader of the Demon Army that I do not know of. It was likely a fight over interdimensional interference. That is why he must have appeared alone now, without the Demon Army.'
His body grew heavier with each step that brought him closer to Kelliark.
When was the best time to strike back.
For the first time since ascending to the state of a Genesis Knight, Jin could not read the perfect moment to swing his sword. It was the same for the other Genesis Knights watching him from afar.
'I cannot tell when to enter to support the youngest... If I go in wrong, the youngest will be in even more danger.'
'Damn it, I have to protect the kid. I can't get a read on him...! The moment I'm off by even a little, it's a fatal wound.'
Van, at least, unlike Luna and Murakan, seemed to see a very faint path.
But it was too hazy to be certain, and in her opinion, there was something more necessary right now than supporting Jin.
Kragos.
She had to secure the ego of the Sun God. Because, at least until now, the reason the Demon Army had not 'eliminated' this world was revealed to be the complete resurrection of the Sun God.
It seemed that capturing Kragos as a hostage had the highest chance of success. However, even as Van tried to pressure Kragos, she couldn't help but remain conscious of Jin's side.
While everyone in the coalition was unable to find their bearings.
Before they knew it, the distance between Jin and Kelliark had narrowed to about a dozen steps. Jin had restrained himself from swinging his sword several times.
At this rate, it felt like he would soon start to run out of breath. Before a ragged breath could escape his lips, he had to make a decision.
“It was a good thing I came in person.”
But suddenly, Kelliark Zipple stopped his steps and opened his mouth.
It was at the point where exactly ten steps remained. The reason he had stopped was because he had no intention of allowing even a small variable to the hegemons of the 677th dimension.

If he were to attack Jin as things were, the Genesis Knights would all rush in at once. Whether it was the perfect moment or not. In that case, Kelliark thought he could not guarantee a 'flawless victory.'
A victory where, for instance, he could defeat them without a single scratch, and make it so they could never counterattack again until the day the war ended.
Now was not the right moment to derive such a victory.
Because, as Jin had predicted, he had fought an invisible war with Malugia while preparing to come to the 677th dimension, and as a result, he had come over to this place alone for the time being.
The Demon Army, and the unified Zipple's complete Origin Stone. He needed to secure those two elements first.

“I do not know how long it has been since I have stopped my steps before an enemy, Jin Runcandel. To think that such a great variable like you all would appear in a wasteland-like dimension like this. It is confusing. Should I appraise you all as great, or should I acknowledge a few immortals...”
Piiik-!
Suddenly, a sharp metallic sound spread.
It was right after Kelliark had waved his hand once in the empty air. He, instead of attacking Jin, had aimed for a figure that was stationary in the air.
“Keok!”
The short, final scream of someone followed.
Because the battlefield was so quiet, everyone could hear that voice. It was the scream of Lagal, the Demon King who had been with Kelliark to the very end.
Ragal had been holding onto the Origin Stone to which Elona was bound and was injecting poison, but from the moment Kelliark appeared, his body had been frozen and he could not move.
Ragal met his end with a hole in his chest, but no one knew what had flown from where to leave that wound.

Furthermore, what was more shocking was the fact that Lagal did not simply turn into a corpse. The moment his chest was pierced, his entire body aged at the speed of light as if he had met eons of time at once, and he was seen decomposing before he even hit the ground.
It was the moment the tenacious life that had survived since the Great Demon World War finally met its end.
'That bastard's magic... no, his authority includes the attribute of handling time. It's at a level that even a contractor of Olta could not dare to fathom.'

As Ragal disappeared, the Origin Stone, which had been soaked in poison and had swollen up, turning a bluish color, began to fall to the floor. At that moment, there was one person in the coalition who moved.
“Lady Elona!”
Veradin Zipple.

With the sole intention of saving Elona, he raised a wind magic and tried to catch the falling Origin Stone. And the moment Veradin shouted, the Genesis Knights naturally intuited that he would be killed by Kelliark.
Because of that, Jin wanted to throw his body towards Veradin at once, but for some reason, he first confirmed that Kelliark was not moving.
'Does he think Veradin is not worth killing? Or else... ah!'
Now, Kelliark's gaze was fixed not on Jin, nor Veradin, nor the other Genesis Knights, but on the Origin Stone that had stopped its fall.
The Origin Stone, which had been engulfed in Ragal's poison, was shining with an unspeakably intense sun energy.
“Yes, Malugia. You've been watching for a chance to strike me for quite a long time. You have to stop me somehow, don't you? Just as all the Malugias who died by my hand did.”
It was Malugia's sun energy.
